anomalies.observed: The only heater-related status LED/resistor pair is D6/R10 on the MCU control net /Microcontroller/NET0016, which is driven by ESP32 GPIO1 and also connected to U4 IN/DIAG_EN. The actual heater output net from U4 OUT to the heater screw terminal J5 pin 2 has no LED or series resistor connected to it.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that a status LED and series resistor are on the HEATER output net, so that the LED visually indicates the actual energized heater output. In the netlist this would require the LED/resistor to be connected to Net-(J5-Pin_2), not to the GPIO1 control net.

evidence.quote: A status LED (`D2`) and series resistor (`R3`) are also on the `HEATER` net, so the heater output doubles as a visual "heater on" indicator at the board level

anomalies.impact: The board LED will light whenever GPIO1 is asserted, even if the TPS1H200 high-side switch is faulted, disabled, or the heater output is not actually energized. This changes the intended behavior from an output-state indicator to a command-state indicator.
